name: Windy & Carl
label: Kranky
lede: A married couple from Dearborn with no drummer, a mountain of delay pedals and a record shop that moved six times, making the slowest, warmest noise in Michigan for three decades.

eras.title: Guitar drones in a Dearborn bedroom
eras.text: Carl Hultgren was already recording long instrumental guitar drones when Windy Weber joined him, and she learned bass from him on the spot. Their home was Detroit's 1990s space-rock underground, a scene that looked to Spacemen 3, Loop and krautrock instead of the Motor City's rock heroes.

years.h: Carl Hultgren starts recording guitar drones alone
years.p: Before the duo existed, Hultgren was taping instrumental drone pieces built from guitar, delay and reverb, with no drums and no synthesizers. That recipe never really changed.

years.h: Windy Weber learns bass on a Mudhoney song, and a duo is born
years.p: Carl Hultgren taught Windy Weber to play bass; the first song she learned was [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]]'s Touch Me I'm Sick. The husband-and-wife pair became Windy & Carl in Dearborn in 1993.
years.xp: Weber told Perfect Sound Forever that the early songs had more structure than what came later, pointing to the 7-inch tracks Dragonfly and Instrumental 1 and 2. Over time the structure melted into long tides of guitar, bass and effects, with Weber's voice floating low in the mix.

years.h: Watersong/Dragonfly: the first single, on their own Blue Flea
years.p: Windy & Carl's debut 7-inch comes out on Blue Flea, the label Weber and Hultgren run themselves. Blue Flea is still putting out their records more than thirty years later.

years.h: Portal: the first album, on Ba Da Bing!
years.p: The debut full-length lands on Ba Da Bing!, the same year Detroit's Burnt Hair Records issues their Instrumentals EP. Burnt Hair and Zoot's Coffeehouse were the hub of the local space-rock scene.

years.h: Antarctica on Darla, Dream of Blue on Ochre
years.p: Two albums in one year on two labels, after 1996's Drawing of Sound on Icon. Windy Weber's voice starts to surface from the haze.

years.h: On tour across Europe with Silver Apples
years.p: Windy & Carl split a single with [[Silver Apples|802d971d-5fb1-4ca1-8e56-69c64122d957]], Crazy in the Sun on Rocket Girl, then tour with them through England, France, Switzerland, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, Norway, Sweden and the Netherlands.

eras.title: The label that Labradford built
eras.text: Windy & Carl wanted to be on Kranky because of Labradford, and in 1998 they got there. A record shop, a side project and a steady stream of Terrastock festival sets followed, and so did a private audience with Sonic Youth.

q: Labradford, who made us want to be on Kranky
years.src: Perfect Sound Forever (2013) · AllMusic · Wikipedia: Kranky
years.h: Depths: Windy & Carl's first album on Kranky
years.p: The Chicago drone label Kranky signs the Dearborn duo. Windy Weber said [[Codeine|cecd5f91-cfdd-45d1-879f-3920c7c76e58]]'s Frigid Stars and Labradford were what made them want the label in the first place.
years.xp: Kranky had been founded in Chicago in 1993 specifically to release [[Labradford|7cf7ef41-9637-4bf2-ae99-d8d6611ccdc6]]'s debut, and the label's slow, patient catalog was exactly where Windy Weber and Carl Hultgren pictured themselves. Depths began a relationship that ran, on and off, for more than twenty years.

q: We work all day, even when we are not in the shop
years.h: Windy Weber and Carl Hultgren open Stormy Records in Dearborn
years.p: The couple starts a record shop that becomes a second career. Stormy Records would move six times in twenty-two years and host in-stores by [[Devendra Banhart|0110e63e-0a9b-4818-af8e-41e180c20b9a]], [[Joanna Newsom|cb69e1f1-bc76-4df5-93c9-cf97dd8a3b5c]] and [[Bonnie 'Prince' Billy|7b0a63b2-b8e8-490e-b724-1d30cb5edfe3]].
years.xp: Weber told Metromode in 2019 that the shop survived downloads and then streaming by keeping personal bills low, picking affordable leases and being careful with every dollar. When things were slow, mail order kept the doors open. By its twentieth year Stormy was at 13306 Michigan Avenue in east downtown Dearborn.

years.h: Five Way Mirror: Windy & Carl add synthesist Greg Gasiorowski
years.p: The couple teams with synth player Greg Gasiorowski under the name Five Way Mirror, releasing several singles and the full-length Transcendence. It's the rare Windy & Carl project with a synthesizer in it.

years.h: A 28-minute jam with The Lothars from Terrastock London
years.p: Windy & Carl release a CD with Boston's [[The Lothars|201debf5-dda7-47cd-bf44-9fce64416264]], built around a 28-minute collaborative piece played at the Terrastock festival in London. The duo became Terrastock regulars.

years.h: Consciousness, then a summer tour with Landing
years.p: Windy & Carl's second Kranky album is followed by a national summer tour with Landing and a split tour CD. The tour's highlight: a private show played just for [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]].

eras.title: Grief, a dog named Flea, and the heartbreak record
eras.text: After a three-CD rarities box, Windy & Carl went quiet when Windy Weber's mother died. They came back with a record dedicated to their late dog and, in 2008, the album many fans now name first.

years.h: Introspection: three CDs of singles, rarities and live tracks
years.p: Blue Flea gathers Windy & Carl's scattered early 7-inches, compilation tracks and live recordings into a three-disc set.

years.h: Windy Weber's mother dies and Windy & Carl go on hiatus
years.p: According to Wikipedia and AllMusic, the band stepped away from recording after Weber's mother died, while the couple kept Stormy Records running.

years.h: The Dream House / Dedications to Flea ends the silence
years.p: Windy & Carl return from hiatus with a record dedicated to Flea, the couple's dog, who had recently died.

years.h: Akimatsuri: one 33-minute track, recorded March to October
years.p: A single 33:16 piece in five movements, built slowly over seven months of 2006 and released on Blue Flea.

years.h: Music for the film August Evening
years.p: Windy & Carl contribute to the score of the indie drama August Evening alongside [[Mono|ffe02aed-ef7e-4736-a186-c2f1dd55ce8d]], Masakatsu Takagi and [[Yellow6|fecd919d-51c1-4451-9599-9070617ceafa]].

years.h: Songs for the Broken Hearted brings Windy Weber's voice forward
years.p: Ten songs on Kranky, with Weber singing more clearly than ever. AllMusic says the album won Windy & Carl renewed attention, helped by praise from younger artists.

eras.title: Shop hours and long drones
eras.text: Records now came when the shop allowed: an instrumental companion, a Kranky album in 2012, homemade singles on Blue Flea. Then 2020 brought a new Kranky record and Jack White's label putting their earliest demo on a Detroit history lesson.

years.h: Instrumentals for the Broken Hearted strips out the vocals
years.p: A Blue Flea companion to Songs for the Broken Hearted, with Windy Weber's voice removed.

years.h: We Will Always Be: Windy & Carl's fourth Kranky album
years.p: The duo's first Kranky full-length in four years, joined the same year by a self-titled four-song mini-album on Blue Flea.

years.h: Blues for a UFO on Blue Flea
years.p: A full-length on the couple's own label, between a string of holiday and odds-and-ends 7-inches.

years.h: Allegiance and Conviction: back on Kranky
years.p: Six long tracks, from The Stranger to Crossing Over, Windy & Carl's first Kranky album since 2012.

years.h: Unreleased Home Recordings 1992–1995, with hand-painted art
years.p: Blue Flea issues a three-CD set of Windy & Carl demos and outtakes from their first four years, each copy with hand-painted artwork.

years.h: Third Man's Southeast of Saturn puts Windy & Carl in Detroit history
years.p: [[Jack White|3ae2fb37-8a23-429d-9920-bac811c4fc22]]'s Third Man Records compiles Detroit's 1990s space-rock scene, with Windy & Carl's Instrumental #2 alongside [[Majesty Crush|0cfd3007-1861-47ea-8255-9a8194af2229]], [[Füxa|0c291615-ff4a-4c55-9404-2a829484c2cc]] and [[Auburn Lull|d733cde0-4e84-4b3e-bfbd-4863939c5b7d]].

eras.title: Closing the shop, opening the amps
eras.text: After twenty-two years Stormy Records closed, and the couple finally had the time Weber had talked about for their own work. A new album and the first shows in years followed.

years.h: Stormy Records closes after 22 years
years.p: Windy Weber and Carl Hultgren shut the Dearborn shop they opened in 1999. Weber had said in 2019 that retiring from the store would mean more time for their own music.

years.h: Heavy Early & The Creation of Venus on Blue Flea
years.p: Windy & Carl's newest full-length, released on the label they started with their first single in 1993.

years.h: Windy & Carl play live again after a long hiatus
years.p: In October 2024 the duo returns to the stage for the first time in years, according to setlist.fm and Wikipedia.
